title: holistic-wait-horizon-adaptive-allocator
author: Ivy Nguyen
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive wait-horizon allocator that reduces starvation and tail latency in the continuous batcher, with kernel hinting for KV-heavy paths and configurable timeout backoff policies.
description: Context: Continuous batcher tail latency and occasional starvation for KV-heavy requests under mixed workloads have caused customer-visible SLO regressions at high concurrency. Motivation: previous fixes focused on slot reservation and static timeouts; we need an allocator that dynamically adapts wait horizons by request-class, KV pin usage, and recent dequeue telemetry to reduce head-of-line blocking without regressing throughput. Summary of changes: implemented a Holistic Wait Horizon allocator that (1) computes per-cohort dynamic wait budgets using an exponential moving average of dequeue latency and recent success rate, (2) applies soft reservations for KV-pinned requests with decay based on observed KV cache hit stability, (3) exposes a jittered timeout backoff and a fast-path preemption token for short requests, and (4) surfaces allocator metrics and knobs in the Console + docs. Implementation notes: new serve/scheduler/horizon_policy.go contains the core adaptive policy with a compact state machine; serve/batcher/allocator.go wires the policy into the admission loop and adds per-request metadata propagation for kernels; serve/kv/cache_pin.go introduces a lightweight pin score estimator that surfaces hints to the allocator; runtime/kernels/quantized_scheduler_hint.cu adds a single kernel-level hint path used by the hot allocator code (no behavioral changes to inference kernels). Safety: allocator uses conservative defaults and a global flag redwood.batcher.horizon.enabled=false to disable the new policy at runtime. Tests & CI: added integration and unit tests (tests/batcher/horizon_allocator_integration_test.go, tests/scheduler/horizon_policy_unit_test.go) and a small end-to-end load replay harness (benchmark/fixtures/mixed-kv-heavy-replay.json). Performance: internal canary on Dedicated pools shows 18-24% reduction in P99 latency for mixed KV workloads and a 3-5% throughput increase under medium contention; CPU overhead measured +2% at controller level. Rollout plan: enabled by default on canary fleet for two weeks then gradual ramp to 25% of Dedicated capacity; fallback to static-batcher on regressions. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1819) | [x] unit tests | [x] integration tests | [x] perf canary report included | [x] docs update | [x] feature flag gate. Related work: complements ENG-2042 (KV pin scoring), replaces earlier temporary hotfix in pr-138502. CI notes: observed flaky test tests/batcher/latency_meter_test during first run; reran and all checks passed. Merge: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.
